chunks: The faithful who sit idle, other than those who are disabled, are not equal to those who fight in the way of God with their wealth and lives. God has exalted those in rank who fight for the faith with their wealth and souls over those who sit idle. Though God's promise of good is for all, He has granted His favour of the highest reward to those who struggle in preference to those who sit at home.

key_terms.أُولُو الضَّرَرِ: Those with a valid excuse or disability
key_terms.الْقَاعِدُونَ: Those who sit idle or remain stationary
key_terms.الْمُجَاهِدُونَ: Those who strive or fight in the way of God
key_terms.بِأَمْوَالِهِمْ وَأَنْفُسِهِمْ: With their wealth and their souls/lives

ai.seo_question: What is the difference in spiritual rank between those who sit idle and those who strive in the way of God?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the virtue of active jihad while acknowledging that the 'sitters' are not entirely excluded from reward, except for those who are disabled (uli al-darar). It underscores the hierarchical merit of those who contribute both materially and physically in God's cause, a concept central to understanding social and spiritual duties in Islamic community life. The exception for the disabled emphasizes that physical inability does not equate to spiritual deficiency, preserving their status among the believers.
